cases.purpose: Combined -cp rejects an unavailable CPU without changing the owned child affinity
cases.oracle: Upstream taskset from the locked VM image, with the same controlled child program on each side.
cases.comparison: Assert EINVAL and unchanged child affinity independently with sched_getaffinity.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/sleep 20 & child=$!
trap 'kill -KILL "$child" 2>/dev/null; wait "$child" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
taskset -cp 5 "$child" > out 2> err; rc=$?; [[ $(<err) == *"Invalid argument"* ]] && d=EINVAL || d=other; printf "status=%s diagnostic=%s\n" "$rc" "$d"; rm -f out err
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os,sys;print("cpus="+",".join(map(str,sorted(os.sched_getaffinity(int(sys.argv[1]))))))' "$child"

cases.purpose: Separate -c -p still sets an owned child affinity
cases.oracle: Upstream taskset from the locked VM image, with the same controlled child program on each side.
cases.comparison: Exact GNU output after replacing only the independently known owned-child PID in verified line prefixes; all affinity formatting remains compared. Python sched_getaffinity independently asserts the precise resulting CPU set.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/sleep 20 & child=$!
trap 'kill -KILL "$child" 2>/dev/null; wait "$child" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
out=$(taskset -c -p 1 "$child"); rc=$?; [[ $rc == 0 ]] || exit 91
printf "%s\n" "$out" | /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import sys
prefix="pid "+sys.argv[1]+"\'"'"'s "
lines=sys.stdin.read().splitlines();assert len(lines)==int(sys.argv[2]),lines
for line in lines:
 assert line.startswith(prefix),line
 print("pid CHILD\'"'"'s "+line[len(prefix):])
' "$child" 2 || exit 92
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os,sys
a=os.sched_getaffinity(int(sys.argv[1]));assert a=={1}
print("cpus="+",".join(map(str,sorted(a))))' "$child"
